newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea's Jan c/a deficit soars to $3.09 bln.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea's Jan c/a deficit soars to $3.09 bln.

text.p: South Korea's current account deficit soared to $3.09 billion in January from a $1.72 billion shortfall a year earlier, preliminary figures from the Bank of Korea (BOK) showed on Tuesday.
Jan 1997 Dec 1996 Jan 1996
Invisible trade -745.0 -859.0 -597.7
NOTE - Figures are in millions of US dollars
The central bank said the country posted a deficit both in trade and invisible trade accounts due to a drop in exports and increased spending by travellers abroad.
Import growth slowed to 6.1 percent year-on-year in January from a 35.9 percent gain a year earlier in line with a slowdown in capital investment.
But the trade deficit widened because exports suffered a year-on-year drop due to strikes at key industries following the passage in December of a controversial labour law.
Exports fell 4.4 percent to $9.84 billion in January while imports rose 6.1 percent to $12.1 billion.
Automobile exports, hardest hit by almost four weeks of strikes, fell 42.9 percent year-on-year in January to $440 million on a customs cleared basis.
A continued slump in semiconductor exports as a result of weak international prices for dynamic random access memory chips also hampered the trade account.
Electronics exports fell 14.9 percent to $1.96 billion in January, compared with a 43.2 percent growth to $2.3 billion a year earlier.
The trade deficit with major trading partners the United States, Japan and the European Union continued to expand.
The customs-cleared deficit with these markets widened to $3.39 billion in January from a $2.12 billion shortfall a year earlier and a $1.38 billion deficit in December.
With other markets, the country's surplus narrowed to $80 million in January from a $710 million surplus a year earlier.
South Korea's Finance and Economy Ministry has forecast this year's current account deficit at about $18 billion, compared with a $23.72 billion shortfall in 1996.
